target: bar-pairing binding observables B_arch(K) and B_bar(K): the archimedean and Hecke-bar lengths of the free-minus-bound character difference
target_value: B_arch(K) = E_0 * sum_lambda y_lambda ( |chi^lambda(W_free)| - |chi^lambda(W_atom)| );  B_bar(K) = E_0 * sum_lambda y_lambda ( ||chi^lambda(W_free)||_bar - ||chi^lambda(W_atom)||_bar ),  ||chi||_bar = sqrt(chi(q_0) chi(q_0^{-1}))
description: Derivation chain for the bar-pairing binding observable (PR #1742, Rust-engine extension #1748) and the two free-configuration chi caches its producer emits alongside it -- 3 witnesses. The construction contrasts TWO length functions on the same per-partition characters: the archimedean modulus at q_0, and the Hecke/KL bar pairing sqrt(chi(q_0) chi(q_0^{-1})). Trust profile: one AXIOM entrypoint (Hecke energy), one CALIBRATION input (E_0, CAL-1), three DERIVED steps, one SCRIPT_CITED frontier. The result is a scope-(a) NEGATIVE and is recorded as one: the bar length underbinds the deuteron by ~70%.

steps.name: Hecke relation and the balanced q-integer
steps.operation: The Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(q) is the braid-group algebra of B_n modulo (sigma_i - q)(sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0; the eigenvalue separation (q - q^{-1}) is the per-crossing Hecke energy scale, the AXIOM entrypoint of every Hecke-side chain. The relation is invariant under the bar involution q <-> q^{-1} up to the sign of that separation, which is what makes the two evaluation points of this chain a matched pair rather than two unrelated anchors.

steps.name: Per-partition characters at q_0 and at q_0^{-1}
steps.operation: Take the per-lambda Hecke characters of the free and bound atomic braid words, chi^lambda(W_free) and chi^lambda(W_atom), evaluated at BOTH the substrate anchor q_0 and its Hecke bar image q_0^{-1}. W_free is the Z+N nucleons each on their own H_3 with no inter-nucleon crossings (include_inter=False); W_atom carries them (include_inter=True). Both are in the averaged / colour-weighted convention.
steps.output_value: { chi^lambda(W_cfg; q) : cfg in {free, atom}, q in {q_0, q_0^{-1}} }
steps.notes: The q_0 side is derivation-backed upstream by chi-at-q0-averaged-atomic.derivation.json, which covers the bound-configuration caches from the same convention. Two of the three witnesses this chain claims ARE the free-configuration half of that same object (chi-{deuteron,helium-4}-free-h{6,12}-at-q0-50dps), emitted by this producer rather than by the hoefsmit one. The q_0^{-1} caches come from chi_at_q_inv_via_native_mpfr.py (PR #1748), which is a separate producer and is NOT claimed here.

steps.name: Bar-symmetrized Wenzl weight y_lambda
steps.operation: Take the canonical Wenzl weight and bar-symmetrize it over the anchor and its image: y_lambda := (y_lambda(q_0) + y_lambda(q_0^{-1})) / 2. The average is real by construction, so the weight does not itself introduce a bar-asymmetry into either observable -- the asymmetry being tested lives entirely in the length function of step 4.

steps.name: Energy scale E_0 = m_e / (q_0 (q_0 - 1))
steps.operation: Fix the MeV scale by the CAL-1 electron mass: E_0 := m_e / (q_0 (q_0 - 1)). This is a calibration input, not a derived quantity -- it is the single place the dimensional unit enters, exactly as the three-calibration discipline requires.
steps.notes: CAL-1 (m_e) sets the unit by fiat. Per the 2026-08-11 absolute-mass excision, the MeV figures below are m_e-scaled REALIZATIONS of a dimensionless ratio, not absolute-mass predictions.

steps.name: Two length functions on the same characters
steps.operation: Define the archimedean length as the modulus at the anchor, |chi^lambda(q_0)| -- at real q_0 the conjugation bar is trivial, so this is the ordinary absolute value. Define the Hecke/KL bar length as the geometric mean across the bar involution, ||chi^lambda||_bar := sqrt( chi^lambda(q_0) * chi^lambda(q_0^{-1}) ). The two coincide only where the character is bar-invariant; the binding observable is their difference of free-minus-bound sums.
steps.notes: Free-minus-bound is the sign convention that makes binding positive: entangling the nucleons LOWERS the summed character length, and the deficit is the binding.

steps.name: Numerical evaluation -- and the bar length underbinds
steps.operation: Evaluate both observables at the substrate anchor and compare to the AME experimental binding. On the deuteron: B_arch = 2.3043266203187662 MeV against AME 2.224566, an error of +3.59%; B_bar = 0.6596730118309209 MeV, an error of -70.35%.
steps.notes:
script: computations/bar_pairing_binding_observable.py -- the frontier step.

SCOPE-(a) NEGATIVE, stated as one: the Hecke/KL bar pairing, USED ALONE AS THE LENGTH FUNCTION, does not reproduce the deuteron binding -- it underbinds by ~70%. That constrains the magnitude of this particular length function; it does NOT exclude the bar pairing as an ingredient of a multi-term closure, and no proved invariant forbids it. The archimedean modulus at +3.59% is the better of the two but is not at the 100x L2 target either.

COVERAGE, recorded rather than smoothed: the witness's own description says it extends the observable 'to T, 3He, 4He', but its `results` array carries the DEUTERON ONLY. The cross-series confirmation the description promises has not been run, so the ~70% figure is a single-nuclide result, not a series finding.

The AME comparison value in the witness (2.224566) predates the 2026-08-19 AME re-derivation; the vendored AME2020 table gives 2.2245662. The 0.2 eV difference does not move the percentages quoted above.
